patches.old: women earn approximately 82 cents for every dollar earned by men (as of recent data), though this figure varies substantially by race, occupation, and education level.
patches.new: the figure depends on which workers are counted, so identify the measure before comparing numbers. On the most recent Census data, women working **full time, year round** earned about **84 cents** for every dollar earned by men, while across **all workers** — including part-time and part-year — the figure is about **78 cents**. The gap also varies substantially by race, occupation and education: measured against white men, Black and Hispanic women's earnings ratios are far lower than the headline figure.

visual.title: Decomposing the gap, and the barriers above it
visual.alt: A reminder to check whether a pay-gap figure counts full-time year-round workers or all workers, followed by four cards for occupational segregation, devaluation, the motherhood penalty against the fatherhood bonus, and the within-job gap. Below, a panel of vertical barriers covering the glass ceiling, glass escalator, sticky floor and double bind, and a panel naming the sex-gender distinction, performativity, patriarchy, intersectionality, minority stress and medicalization.
visual.caption: If sorting into occupations explained the whole gap, the within-occupation gap would be zero — and it is not.
